item.description:
Etna 1.3 (build 5)

Notes before the meeting starts, a redesigned onboarding, and a clearer Summary setup.

  • Pre-meeting notes: a notes icon in the notch's top-left corner opens a scratchpad before anything is recording — and you keep typing on the same Notes tab once the meeting starts. Type "- " for bullets, ⌘B/⌘I for bold and italic.
  • Summary settings, rebuilt around brand tiles: pick Apple Intelligence, Claude, OpenAI, or Gemini as your summarizer, with key status and setup right below the tiles.
  • Onboarding, redesigned: the Etna stone up front, more breathing room, provider tiles on the AI step, and Skip tucked into the notch's corner.
  • Settings panes that need your attention — a missing permission, a folder that isn't a vault — now show an orange dot in the sidebar.
  • A returning speaker is recognized as themselves instead of appearing as a duplicate "Speaker N", and a half-edited name can no longer stick by accident.
  • Meetings where nothing was transcribed end with a calm one-line notice, and first launch now suggests transcription languages from your keyboard layouts.

Etna 1.2 (build 4)

A living map of the people you meet, effortless back-to-back meetings, and a feedback channel.

  • Stakeholder map: Etna keeps a note per person you meet regularly in a People/ folder of your vault — their meetings, action items, groups, and "often seen with" links — so Obsidian's graph shows your relationship network. Your own edits are never touched.
  • Back-to-back meetings run themselves: when the next meeting starts while the last one is still summarizing, Etna hands off and begins recording within seconds. Deferred auto-record catches up the moment the app is free.
  • Over-split speakers can now be merged in the "who said what" review — pick "Merge into" from a row's menu.
  • What's New (this window!) opens once after each update, and lives in Settings → General → Updates.
  • Send Feedback… in the ⋯ menu: a pre-filled email to support, with an optional diagnostics report that never includes meeting content.
  • Optional anonymous usage analytics — strictly opt-in, off unless you say yes, and never anything you said, wrote, or named.

Etna 1.1 (build 3)

Live translation, a natural guide voice, and language detection you can tune.

  • Live translation: flip the Translate switch during a meeting and the transcript bubbles appear in your chosen language — translated on this Mac, nothing leaves the device. Your saved note always keeps what was actually spoken.
  • Etna's guide now speaks with a natural recorded voice instead of the system synthesizer.
  • Choose which languages automatic detection listens for (up to four, in your order of preference) in Settings → Transcription.
  • Language detection is harder to fool: similar-sounding languages no longer split the vote.
  • Updates got quieter: a new version shows as a gentle hint in the notch and never interrupts a meeting in progress.
